extracted.intended_audience: programmers and TeX users writing MetaPost graphics and macros
extracted.subtask_description: Authoring and manipulating MetaPost drawings, pens, pictures, glyph extraction, and macros — including use of primitive drawing commands, picture inspection, and macro parameter conventions. Covers practical constraints and semantics needed to produce correct MetaPost output and reusable macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of drawing options
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing options affect only those statements where they make sense (e.g., "The dashed ⟨dash pattern⟩ option only affects draw ⟨path expression⟩ statements, and text appearing in the ⟨picture expression⟩ argument to draw ⟨picture expression⟩ statement is only affected by the withcolor ⟨color expression⟩ option").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying options, ensure they are appropriate for the target drawing statement (dashed applies to draw path only; withcolor in a draw picture affects only text in the picture). For mixed-picture draws, expect some options to affect parts of the picture but not others.

rubrics_metrics.name: currentpen semantics and equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a special pen variable called currentpen such that fill ... withpen currentpen is equivalent to a filldraw statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use currentpen to refer to the last pen picked up; understand equivalences (fill withpen currentpen ↔ filldraw) when translating between high-level and primitive forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: beginfig and default pen
rubrics_metrics.description: beginfig resets the current pen to a default value of pencircle scaled 0.5bp at the beginning of each figure; this can be reselected at any time by pickup defaultpen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on persistent pen state across figures; explicitly pickup desired pen inside a figure if not using the default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pen shapes and transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: pencircle scaled ⟨numeric⟩ produces lines of specified width; applying affine transformations (xscaled, yscaled, rotated, etc.) yields elliptical/calligraphic pen shapes so that line width depends on line orientation relative to the pen's axes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get calligraphic effects, transform pencircle using affine operators; be aware that visual stroke width varies with stroke direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pen edge operators (lft/rt/top/bot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators lft, rt, top, and bot answer where the left/right/top/bottom edge of the current pen would be when placed at a position; they also accept pair arguments and compute the x and y coordinates of extremal points on the pen shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these operators for precise placement and to compute offsets based on the actual pen bounding box (examples show numeric offsets like 0.0867in).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polygonal pens and makepen/pensquare
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost allows polygonal pen shapes; pensquare is predefined and equivalent to makepen((-.5,-.5)--(.5,-.5)--(.5,.5)--(-.5,.5)--cycle). The makepen operator takes a convex-polygon-shaped path and makes a pen of that shape and size; non-convex or non-polygonal paths are straightened/deduped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use makepen to create custom polygonal pens; note that makepen/pensquare should not be used with dash patterns (compatibility warning).

rubrics_metrics.name: makepath inverse of makepen
rubrics_metrics.description: The inverse of makepen is makepath that takes a ⟨pen primary⟩ and returns the corresponding path (e.g., makepath pencircle produces fullcircle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use makepath when you need to inspect or reuse the geometric outline of a pen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive drawing command syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Primitive drawing statements let you specify a picture variable to hold results. Syntax includes addto⟨picture variable⟩also⟨picture expression⟩⟨option list⟩, addto⟨picture variable⟩contour⟨path expression⟩⟨option list⟩, addto⟨picture variable⟩doublepath⟨path expression⟩⟨option list⟩ and an ⟨option list⟩ grammar (withcolor, withpen, dashed, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When precise control over where output goes is required, use primitive addto forms rather than high-level draw/fill which always write to currentpicture. Consult the option-list grammar for available drawing options.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-level drawing → primitive expansion and option appending
rubrics_metrics.description: Each high-level statement (draw, fill, etc.) expands to primitives that append their own ⟨option list⟩; an option appended to the primitive is equivalent to appending it to the high-level statement's option list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of how expansions apply default options (e.g., draw expands to addto currentpicture doublepath p withpen currentpen) and that appending options to the primitive or high-level form is equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: withpen option overriding behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple withpen options arise (for example from expansion plus an explicit withpen), the later withpen silently overrides the earlier one (e.g., addto currentpicture doublepath p withpen currentpen withpen pencircle — the second overrides the first).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ambiguity by explicitly specifying the desired pen last, and be mindful that implicit withpen from expansions can be overridden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping of common drawing statements to primitives
rubrics_metrics.description: Table mapping draw p, draw pic, fill c, filldraw c, undraw, unfill, etc., to their equivalent primitive forms (addto currentpicture doublepath/contour ... withpen 𝑞 withcolor 𝑏, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the table to convert between convenient high-level statements and explicit primitives when you need to construct or manipulate picture variables directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: clip primitive and clipping usage
rubrics_metrics.description: clip ⟨picture variable⟩ to ⟨path expression⟩ trims the contents of the picture variable to eliminate everything outside the cyclic path. There is no high-level version, so use clip currentpicture to ⟨path⟩ to clip the current picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember to call clip on the intended picture variable. Clipping affects the contents and later inspections of that picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: shipout behavior and file naming
rubrics_metrics.description: shipout ⟨picture expression⟩ writes a picture as a PostScript file whose file name is determined by outputtemplate; by default the file name ends .nnn where nnn is the decimal representation of charcode. beginfig sets charcode and endfig invokes shipout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the outputtemplating and charcode convention when automating figure generation; ensure proper beginfig/endfig usage so shipout occurs as expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: image macro to capture drawing output
rubrics_metrics.description: image( ⟨drawing commands⟩ ) takes as input a sequence of arbitrary drawing operations and returns a picture variable containing the corresponding output, without affecting currentpicture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use image when you want to create reusable picture objects without disturbing the main currentpicture (e.g., define wheel := image( ... )).

rubrics_metrics.name: for ... within iteration over picture components
rubrics_metrics.description: for ⟨symbolic token⟩ within ⟨picture expression⟩: iterates components of a picture in the order they were drawn. The component for clipping or setbounds paths includes everything the path applies to; if a single clipping applies to the whole picture, the iteration ignores the enclosing clipping or setbounds path to make contents accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this iteration to inspect and manipulate picture components; be mindful of how clipping/setbounds affect component granularity and iteration results.

rubrics_metrics.name: length ⟨picture⟩ returns number of components
rubrics_metrics.description: length ⟨picture primary⟩ returns the number of components that a for ... within iteration would find.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use length to size arrays or loops when processing picture components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component-type predicate operators
rubrics_metrics.description: stroked ⟨primary⟩, filled ⟨primary⟩, textual ⟨primary⟩, clipped ⟨primary⟩, and bounded ⟨primary⟩ test whether the first component of a picture is a stroked line, filled outline, piece of typeset text, clipping path, or setbounds path respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the type predicate before using part extraction operators to avoid non-meaningful queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-extraction operators for stroked/filled/textual components
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is a picture and stroked p is true, then pathpart p is the stroked path, penpart p is the pen used, dashpart p is the dash pattern (dashpart returns an empty picture if not dashed). For textual components: textpart p gives the text, fontpart p the font; xpart/ypart/xxpart/xypart/yxpart/yypart report text transforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct part operator corresponding to the component type. dashpart is meaningful only for stroked lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: colorpart and color model identification
rubrics_metrics.description: colorpart ⟨item⟩ returns the color of a component in its respective color model; the color model of a component can be identified by the colormodel operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before extracting color components (redpart, cyanpart, etc.), check colormodel to know which color part operators are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-meaningful part extraction rules (silent defaults)
rubrics_metrics.description: Asking for non-meaningful parts of an item (e.g., redpart of a clipping path, textpart of a stroked item, pathpart of a textual item) is silently accepted and returns a null value or black color component. Specific null returns: trivial path (0,0) for pathpart, nullpen for penpart, empty picture for dashpart, null string for textpart/fontpart, zero for colormodel and most color parts, one for blackpart, and black in current default model for colorpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code that queries parts should handle null/default returns gracefully. These queries do not raise errors except for explicit color-model mismatches (see next).

rubrics_metrics.name: Color part operator model-mismatch behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly asking for a color part of a colored item in the wrong color model returns a black color component and triggers an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always check colormodel before using redpart/greypart/cyanpart etc.; catching or avoiding these errors is necessary when programmatically inspecting pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clipped/bounded component extraction semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: When clipped p or bounded p is true, pathpart p gives the clipping or setbounds path and the other part extraction operators are not meaningful; such non-meaningful extractions return null values (see the listed defaults) but do not generate errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat clipped/bounded components specially — most part extraction other than pathpart is not meaningful and will return defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glyph operator identification and argument rules
rubrics_metrics.description: glyph ⟨numeric expression⟩ of ⟨string expression⟩ or glyph ⟨string expression⟩ of ⟨string expression⟩ identifies a glyph to be converted into a picture. If numeric, it must be an integer slot 0..255 (fractions rounded); out-of-range slots trigger an error. The second argument is the font name looked up in the font map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numeric slots for encoding-based access or CharString names for direct access; ensure a fontmapline or fontmapfile entry exists for the font.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glyph operator output and transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: The glyph operator returns a picture of the glyph's contours filled black and white in greyscale, with contours sorted (black contours before white), directions reversed (so black becomes counter-clockwise), duplicate closing points removed when appropriate, and scaled so one font design unit equals one PostScript point (bp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that returned glyph pictures are processed to approximate font rendering (winding rules not fully implemented), and internals like contour orientation, ordering, and scaling are changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: glyph operator failure modes
rubrics_metrics.description: The glyph operator returns an empty picture if the .tfm or .pfb file cannot be found, if the encoding in the font map cannot be found, if the slot number is not covered by the encoding, or if the CharString name cannot be found. A font map entry is mandatory for the font for glyph to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide correct fontmap entries (fontmapline/fontmapfile) and verify font resources are available; otherwise glyph returns empty without further glyph data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flattening and hinting loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Converting text into plain curves (flattening) loses all hinting information in fonts; flattened text may look distorted on low-resolution output devices. In SVG output, all text is automatically flattened if the internal variable prologues is set to 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid flattening when targeting low-resolution preview unless necessary, or be prepared for degraded appearance; set prologues appropriately for SVG exports that require flattened outlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro definition basics (def and vardef)
rubrics_metrics.description: def ⟨symbolic token⟩ = ⟨replacement text⟩ enddef makes a token an abbreviation. vardef ⟨generic variable⟩ begins a vardef macro that behaves like a variable of type 'macro' and supports multi-token/generic subscript names; vardef automatically inserts begingroup/endgroup around the replacement text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use def for simple macros and vardef when you need generic subscript names or automatic grouping semantics; remember vardef creates implicit grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro parameter types (expr, suffix, text)
rubrics_metrics.description: In macro definitions: expr parameters accept arbitrary expressions (numeric/pair/color/etc.), suffix parameters accept variable names/suffixes, and text parameters accept arbitrary token sequences which are treated as statements when executed inside the macro (e.g., hide(text t) executes t and results in empty output).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose parameter kinds according to intended use: expr for computed values, suffix for passing variable names, text for passing code snippets. Be mindful that text params must be followed by a right parenthesis in calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping and local variables (begingroup/endgroup and save)
rubrics_metrics.description: A group (begingroup ... endgroup) can act like a function call if it ends with an expression, and variables can be made local by save ⟨symbolic token list⟩ which makes all variables starting with the tokens unknown numerics and saves/restores their values at group end. beginfig uses begingroup to provide local variables per figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use groups and save to avoid name collisions and provide local state inside macros or figures. If save is used outside a group, original values are discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim for internal variables
rubrics_metrics.description: save cannot be used to make local changes to MetaPost's internal variables. Use interim ⟨internal variable⟩ := ⟨numeric/string expression⟩ to temporarily set an internal variable and restore it at the end of the group (example: interim linecap:=butt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When temporarily changing internal interpreter variables (linecap, etc.) use interim inside a group to avoid losing their special meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: If-test syntax and usage in macros
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic if test syntax is if ⟨boolean expression⟩: ⟨balanced tokens⟩ elseif ... else ... fi. If tests are not statements and their balanced tokens can be any balanced token sequence; nested/short forms are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use if/elseif/else/fi for conditional logic inside expr macros as well as statements; remember the syntactic flexibility to embed token sequences that are not full statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter passing and call syntax nuances
rubrics_metrics.description: Macro call parameters can be separated by commas or by )( pairs. A text parameter must be followed by a right parenthesis. For example, foo(a,b)(c) vs foo(a,b,c) differ when the macro expects a text parameter followed by an expr parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully match call syntax to definition parameter kinds; use )( separation when text parameters are involved to avoid mixing them with subsequent expr parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vardef special suffix parameters (#@ and @) and name-based behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Every vardef macro has implicit suffix parameters #@ and @ where @ is the last token in the macro call name and #@ is everything preceding the last token. These provide a way for the macro to behave differently depending on the numeric suffix used in the call (e.g., a[]b becomes a2b → #@=a2, @=b). Also vardef ⟨generic variable⟩@# looks for a suffix following the macro name and makes it available as @#.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use #@ and @ to write macros that adapt to the calling name or numeric subscripts; use str @ to extract numeric parts from suffixes when necessary, but prefer avoiding string parsing unless required.
